svg.data-what: one nephron, the unit of the kidney, drawn unrolled: the glomerulus and its capsule in the cortex, the tubule diving into the medulla and back, the collecting duct

rect.data-what: the renal cortex, where the glomeruli and the convoluted tubules lie
the renal medulla, where the loops of Henle and the collecting ducts run down toward the papilla

g.data-what: the peritubular capillaries and vasa recta, taking back what the tubules reabsorb

path.data-what: the venule, carrying the blood away toward the renal vein
the collecting duct, gathering urine from many nephrons; antidiuretic hormone sets how much water it lets back
the proximal convoluted tubule: it takes back most of the water, all the glucose and amino acids, and much of the salt
the loop of Henle, diving into the medulla and back: it builds the salt gradient that lets the kidney concentrate urine
the distal convoluted tubule: fine-tunes salt, potassium and acid; it returns to touch its own glomerulus
Bowman's capsule, the double-walled cup around the glomerulus

circle.data-what: Bowman's space, where the filtrate collects before entering the tubule

g.data-what: the glomerulus, a ball of capillaries where blood pressure pushes water and small molecules out into the capsule: the filter

path.data-what: the afferent arteriole, bringing blood into the glomerulus
the efferent arteriole, narrower, leaving the glomerulus: its narrowness keeps the filtering pressure up
the juxtaglomerular apparatus, where the distal tubule touches the afferent arteriole: it senses salt and releases renin
